paragraphs: A student of Rava, as in [Kiddushin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32b.2): that Rava was serving drinks at the wedding feast of his son, and handed a cup to Rav Pappa and to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and they stood up before him; and to Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda, and they did not stand up before him. Rava became angry and said: Are these rabbis and those not rabbis? (But some read there: Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, the sons of Rav Chisda.)

He was a colleague of Rav Zevid (a student of Rava), disagreeing with him, as in [Bava Batra 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.96a.9) and [Bava Batra 134b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.134b.13) and [Sotah 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.40a.3-4). And we find in [Chullin 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.117a.8): Rav Mari said to Rav Zevid ... he said to him: Of you Scripture says, etc.
And in [Berakhot 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24a.14), he asked Rav Pappa who answered him jokingly, "hair, hair."
And we find in [Zevachim 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.29b.8-9) that Rav Ashi raised a difficulty against him, and Hyman infers there that he was like a teacher of Rav Ashi.

So too he is mentioned in Bava Kamma 39b as cited by Hyman, resolving the words of Abaye,[^4] and in [Yevamot 80a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.80a.4) raising an objection against the words of Rav Yosef, and in [Ketubot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33b.7) challenging the solutions of Rabbi Yaakov of Nehar Pekod.
And in [Shabbat 155b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.155b.12) he says the figurative saying: "anoint its [the dog’s] ears, and then a stick behind it,"[^3]

notes.text: Berakhot24a explicitly has Rav Mari asking Rav Pappa, so מר״פ here means “from Rav Pappa.” Shabbat155b has “anoint its ears”; Hyman’s supplied אורניה differs from the named text’s אודניה. The small food portion/ears image is retained as a proverb. The variant making both Mari and Pinchas sons of Rav Chisda remains explicit.

Kiddushin 32b directly has the rebuke as a question and uses a singular patronymic for Pinchas; Hyman also reports the plural reading. Berakhot 24a directly has Mari asking Rav Pappa and the “hair, hair” reply. Shabbat 155b has the ears-and-stick image in the small-portion-for-a-dog context. Hyman’s teacher inference about Rav Ashi remains an inference, not a new authority relation.

Zevachim gives Mari transmitting in Rabbi Yannai’s name and Rav Ashi raising an objection. Hyman infers a teacher relationship. The consulted Kiddushin gives a singular patronymic after Pinchas, beside the plural reading Hyman reports.

Abaye begins the discussion at the end of [Bava Kamma 38b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.38b.16). In the continuation at [Bava Kamma 39a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.39a.2), Rav Mari explains why giving the fine to the poor would leave it without a specific claimant.
